why: Inserting the predicate–argument guideline caused the scorer to prefer keeping verbs/auxiliaries attached to some arguments, which improved cut quality on long pieces (positive gains in the ≤10 and ≤99 bins) but led to more micro‑splits and earlier cuts in short spans (negative mean in ≤3–≤7), so the net change was near zero and slightly negative on short pieces. The single insertion therefore shifted behaviour toward preserving predicate chunks in long sentences but inadvertently encouraged fragmenting or separating subjects/auxiliaries in short pieces.
lesson: When adding a predicate‑preservation guideline, ensure it doesn't encourage creating very short fragments or splitting subjects from their verbs in short spans — preserve predicate wholes for long contexts without introducing micro‑splits in short pieces.
